D8: event-driven execution (binding architecture rule)
nodes.rationale: Recommendation-only conventions decay exactly when schedule pressure appears and coupling decisions are the expensive-to-reverse kind, so the rule is binding text (ARCHITECTURE.md §3 / ADR D8): all inter-module communication as events or explicit async interfaces, no polling, no shared mutable state, backpressure at every boundary; a static cross-module-call gate is deferred to M2.

nodes.label: gateway@1 primitive contract (9 gateway primitives)
nodes.rationale: keychain split into keychainGet/keychainSet so read/write permission separation works like the fs split; fsScope added as the explicit authorization primitive; names kept platform-neutral (fsScope over Apple's fsBookmark); .d.ts for TS call signatures and JSON Schema only for data files; breaking a frozen shape costs a major version bump - that friction is the product.

nodes.label: Install transaction + append-only receipts journal (data protocols)
D5: contract-first freeze
nodes.rationale: Code-first freezes set de-facto shapes under time pressure that later get retrofitted as 'the contract'; contract/ must freeze before implementation lands so the four platforms (iOS/Android/HarmonyOS/desktop interop) do not drift and capability negotiation has a versioned referent.

nodes.label: Upstream agent spine (ctx.sessions / agents / agentLoop / tools / systemPrompt / projections)
Structured gateway/unimplemented envelope (fail-loud policy)
nodes.rationale: Unclaimed endpoints answer a structured envelope (HTTP 200, error riding inside) instead of hanging or faking; the one-to-one manifest pins the unavailability as evidence - claiming half a surface would trade structured-unavailable honesty for a half-working path.

nodes.label: vendor/ensure-dsh.sh sha256 pin table (untracked vendored trees)
D9: upstream-port discipline
nodes.rationale: At 0.1.x upstream velocity, ported-by-hand flows fork product behavior and guarantee divergence; the real DSH harness is vendored verbatim with all platform difference in in-house shim/glue layers (system support), never edited upstream copies.

nodes.label: D6: verbatim-upstream discipline (pinned vendors)
nodes.rationale: Vendored packages are re-fetched and byte-diffed against pinned tarballs; trees stay UNTRACKED so content gates never judge upstream bytes (which cannot be refactored to satisfy checkers); platform differences belong in the shim layer, never in edits to vendored copies.

nodes.label: upstream/llm-transport.js gateway httpFetch LlmAdapter
nodes.rationale: dsh-llm-deepseek is a desktop direct-fetch transport; the adapter mirrors its wire semantics (finish mapping, SSE contract, usage disambiguation) with gateway httpFetch as the seam so a later re-pin keeps the same shape; no transport-free fallback - a boot without options.llm fails loud.

nodes.label: Official client bundles (58-package application tier, presentation/official-web/client-bundles/)
nodes.rationale: The application tier is a published package face, not a byte format; bundles are built by upstream's own client-face build (build:lib:host / build:lib:client) at the same pin - a custom vite/rollup bundling would be our own build of upstream sources, a fork by another name; a partial roster cannot boot because assertEntriesActive requires all rows.

nodes.label: Chunked web.plugins delivery (ArkTS watchdog fix)
nodes.rationale: A single ~6.9 MB web.plugins bus line blocked the ArkTS main thread past the platform's 6s watchdog (THREAD_BLOCK_6S); web-boot.js accepts a chunked delivery (chunked/final flags, 4-package chunks with event-loop yields) while the iOS single-delivery shape stays untouched.

nodes.label: Cordis Loader service (single, decorated by web-boot)
nodes.rationale: Two cordis Loaders in one context conflict on the loader fiber property (cordis refuses a second claim); web-boot's mountClientModules DECORATES the real Loader's entries()/internal faces with the staged web-plugin rows instead of claiming loader, so AgentPresets and the client composition read the same tree.

nodes.label: ishRun contract primitive (contract/ v1.3.0)
nodes.rationale: iOS forbids child processes and the architecture refuses subprocesses (D2); jitless V8 has no WebAssembly at all; wasmRun is a pure-function ABI that cannot open a file; an in-process emulated Alpine userland (one program per call, child of guest init, exit via zombie) inherits apk/pip/npm as-is with no second OS.
